title: Bringing, Getting, Waiting, Buying
label: ch:pt-bringing-getting-waiting-buying
canDo: I can say that I bring, get, wait for and buy in Portuguese, use conseguir for managing to do a thing, let esperar carry waiting, hoping and expecting at once, and tell comprar's Latin root from the identically spelled one behind English compare.

payoff.summary: The chapter's last lesson closes the set: after comprar the reader produces all four first-person forms in one run - trago, consigo, espero, compro - separates the comparare that gave comprar (com- + parare, 'to procure') from the identically spelled comparare that gave English compare (com- + par, 'equal'), and re-reads tenho comprado as 'I have been buying', not 'I have bought'.
